description: Write one specification from a template held in this binary to a new file. Every value a person must own (the project name, every citation) is left empty, which validate refuses by name and path until it is filled. Never overwrites

out.description: The file to write; it must not exist (a file, directory, FIFO or symlink there is refused). No directory is created

template.description: The template: i2c-spi-bench (examples/sentinel-02-bench.json: a 2-layer STM32H753 board with one I2C sensor and one SPI sensor)

name: init

description: Validate one JSON Specification read from stdin, or from --file

file.description: Read the specification from this file instead of stdin

name: validate

description: Solve one Specification's pins and print the SolvedTopology
name: solve

description: Validate and solve one Specification, then write its KiCad schematic, bill of materials and placed board into a directory

out.description: The directory to write <project_name>.kicad_sch, <project_name>.bom.csv and <project_name>.kicad_pcb into; created if absent

name: emit

description: Validate and solve one Specification, then write everything it produces into an empty or absent directory: kicad/ (as emit writes it), and board/, the board crate with its firmware crate in board/firmware/ and the Renode platform board/<project_name>.repl. Starts no process. With a subcommand, generate one artifact instead (hwdef)

out.description: The directory to write into; it must be empty or absent

name: generate

description: Write ArduPilot's hwdef.dat for a SolvedTopology, from the topology and the parts tables alone (AET-WO-4400b). Starts no process

out.description: Where to write hwdef.dat; it must not exist

name: generate_hwdef

description: Build a board crate's firmware/ crate offline for the part, in the sandbox, and print the verdict with the ELF's sha256

crate.description: The board crate directory, holding firmware/. It is copied, minus a top-level target/, and the copy is built

out.description: Where to write the ELF; it must not exist

name: build

description: Regenerate everything from one Specification into scratch, run every gate on exactly those bytes, and print one verdict naming every artifact's hash and every gate's result

against.description: First compare this directory with the generated tree, byte for byte; any difference fails and no gate runs

against-fab.description: Requires --scenarios. Derive the fabrication package again and compare it with this directory, file by file; any file that differs, is missing or is extra fails

fab-out.description: Requires --scenarios (INV-03 counts the fault campaign). Only if every gate passes, write the fabrication package (Gerbers, drill, placement, BOM, firmware ELF, FAB-NOTES.md, MANIFEST.json) into this directory, which must be empty or absent; the verdict names every file's sha256

scenarios.description: Fault scenarios whose base is --spec, run as campaign runs them

name: verify

description: Bound each I2C line's capacitance, and each SPI bus's SCK and MOSI, from above from a routed board's copper, and judge each bound against the specification's declared bound. Runs no tool

spec.description: The specification whose lines are judged

name: extract

description: KiCad's design rule check on a board (kicad-cli pcb drc)

schematic.description: Also check the board against this .kicad_sch (KiCad's schematic parity). It is copied beside the board and judged with it

spec.description: Judge by the rules this specification declares, and first refuse a board that is not its declared board (copper layers, planes, thickness, through vias); without it, by KiCad's defaults. Either way the gate writes every rule file itself

name: check_drc

description: KiCad's electrical rule check on a schematic (kicad-cli sch erc)
name: check_erc

description: The MCU's support network (AET-WO-4300g): KiCad's netlist of the schematic (kicad-cli sch export netlist) judged against the MCU's row and the specification, each bounded capacitor measured on the board. Never reads the emitter's choices

board.description: The .kicad_pcb file: where each pad sits, for the bounded distances

schematic.description: The .kicad_sch file, whose netlist KiCad exports

spec.description: The specification: the MCU's part and supply, its domains and its connectors

name: check_support

description: Judge what a linked STM32H753 firmware writes to its GPIO registers at reset (gpio_default_config in the ELF) against a SolvedTopology: forward, reverse and package. Starts no process

allow.description: A declared allow-list: pins outside the topology the firmware may configure, each exactly as declared, and why

elf.description: The linked firmware ELF (ELF32, little-endian, EM_ARM)

hwdef-h.description: ArduPilot's generated hwdef.h: its VAL_GPIOx_MODER/AFRL/AFRH must equal the ELF's, or the check refuses

topology.description: The SolvedTopology JSON the firmware was meant to realise

name: check_pinout

description: Each generated pin's output speed against DS12117 Table 149: SPI SCK and MOSI judged at their declared rate, supply and load; every other line named with why it is out of scope. No tool runs
name: check_speeds

description: Prove one Kani harness in a crate and print the verdict

crate.description: The crate directory. It is copied, minus a top-level target/, and the copy is judged

harness.description: The harness to prove: its name, or its path such as proofs::add_in_range. It must name exactly one harness

spec.description: The specification the crate is judged against: the verdict's harness_provenance is `generated` only when the crate is byte for byte the board crate `generate` writes for it

name: prove

description: Load a platform in Renode, list the machine it built, and print the verdict

archive.description: Archive the input run in DIR, a new directory named by its run id (trace 20), which `replay --archive` re-judges with no file. Needs --input

firmware.description: Boot this ELF on the platform and judge the boot by the specification. Needs --spec, and --for or --foreign

for.description: The virtual time the boot runs: an integer with ns, us or ms, at most 100ms on every board, a whole number of 10 ns instructions. Needs --firmware

foreign.description: Judge the boot as a foreign firmware's, one this project did not generate (AET-WO-4400e): declared here, never inferred from the ELF; the verdict's boot says judge foreign. Its value is the virtual time the boot runs, as --for's, at most the foreign window. Needs --firmware; not with --for

input.description: A declared input for a foreign run (AET-WO-4400i): a JSON file of timed MAVLink 2 frames for one declared serial port, sent at their stated virtual times, the board at rest. Its sha256 is the verdict's; a frame that is not MAVLink, forces the arm or skips a check is refused by name. Needs --foreign

platform.description: A .repl file, or @path inside Renode's own tree, such as @platforms/boards/nucleo_h753zi.repl. With --firmware, it must be exactly the platform emitted for --spec

spec.description: The specification the boot is judged by. Needs --firmware

name: simulate

description: Run each fault scenario through simulate --firmware's path, archive every record of each run, and print one JSON line per scenario, then a summary

archive.description: The archive directory; each run is a new directory inside it, named by its run id

firmware.description: The firmware ELF every scenario boots

scenarios.description: The scenario files, run in the order given. Each names its base specification relative to its own directory, inside the current directory

name: campaign

description: Replay one archived run from its trace alone, and print its state-sequence hash: a campaign run's verdict, or for a foreign input run (simulate --foreign --input --archive) its input_verdict, the input's witness re-judged from the trace, which is not the run's verdict
name: replay

description: Attribute one archived campaign run to the electrical or the software half, from its trace alone, naming the rule and the evidence events
name: attribute

description: Propose a specification change for one archived campaign run, from its attribution, and write it (or a generator report, or why nothing is proposed) into an empty directory. Never applies a change or edits a gate

out.description: The directory to write proposal.json, and proposed-spec.json or generator-report.json, into; it must be empty or absent

scenario.description: The scenario file the run ran: the same bytes, with its base resolved as campaign resolves it

name: propose

description: Report whether this host can run every subcommand: the binary's version, the sandbox the tools would run in, the scratch directory, and each external tool's version, naming each missing piece and the subcommands it blocks
name: doctor
